title: Hang a wall cabinet on its French cleat
instruction: Hang the cabinet on the wall: lift it by both side panels, carry it level to the wall with its cleat above the wall cleat, lower it so the cleats hook together, then let go.
context: Carpenters and cabinet installers (O*NET 47-2031.00 Carpenters; 51-7011.00 Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters) hang wall cabinets, shelving and tool panels on French cleats: a 45-degree bevelled strip on the wall and a matching one on the cabinet's back, which wedge the cabinet against the wall once hooked. The cabinet has nothing to hold in its middle, and its cleat has to drop behind the wall cleat along its whole length at once, so it is lifted by both sides, kept level and lowered onto the cleat with both hands.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them; heights from the table top. A fixed wall (60 cm wide, 25 cm tall) stands with its face 44 cm forward. A fixed pine cleat, 40 cm long, 1.5 cm thick and 3 cm tall, is fixed to it, centred on the centre line, its sharp top edge 11 cm above the table and its top bevelled at 45 degrees down toward the wall. A loose pine wall cabinet (an open-fronted shelf box, 32.4 cm wide, 11.5 cm deep and 12 cm tall, 0.8 kg: back, two 12 mm side panels and a bottom) stands upright on the table, centred 30 cm forward on the centre line with its back to the wall; along the top of its back is a matching 1.5 cm cleat, bevelled at 45 degrees down toward the wall, and along the bottom of its back a 1.5 cm spacer. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler and a spirit level; partial credit is the best stage reached during the run, except that if the cabinet tips over (more than 30 degrees) the score is 0 for the rest of the run. 1.0: the cabinet hung on the cleat (its back within 3 mm of the wall cleat's face and its cleat within 3 mm of resting on the wall cleat, within 3 cm of the centre line, level within 1.5 degrees), both grippers let go and at least 5 cm from the cabinet, still for 1 s. 0.75: the cabinet hung on the cleat and level, before the grippers have let go and moved clear, or before it is still. 0.5: the cabinet's cleat right above the wall cleat (within 1 cm of the hung position front to back, at most 4 cm above it), level within 5 degrees. 0.25: the cabinet lifted off the table, level within 5 degrees. 0.0: anything else.
reset_notes: Lift the cabinet off the cleat and stand it back on the table, centred 30 cm forward with its back to the wall; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the cabinet is one rigid body; each cleat's bevel is a thin plate on its 45-degree face; pine on pine has dry friction 0.5; the wall and its cleat are fixed in place (screwed to the wall in reality).
